title: The Sick Stag
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Stag fell sick and lay in a clearing in the forest, too weak to move from the spot. When the news of his illness spread, a number of the other beasts came to inquire after his health, and they one and all nibbled a little of the grass that grew round the invalid till at last there was not a blade within his reach. In a few days he began to mend, but was still too feeble to get up and go in search of fodder; and thus he perished miserably of hunger owing to the thoughtlessness of his friends.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where did the sick Stag lie?
options: In a clearing in the forest
Beside a riverbank
In a farmer's barn
Under a rocky overhang

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why couldn't the Stag move from the spot at first?
options: He was tangled in vines
He was too weak
He was guarding his young
He was asleep

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why did the other beasts come to the Stag?
options: To inquire after his health
To warn him of a hunter nearby
To ask him to lead them
To trade food with him

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the visiting beasts do to the grass around the Stag?
options: They trampled it flat
They nibbled it until none was left within his reach
They avoided it out of respect
They planted new grass for him

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happened to the Stag after a few days?
options: He recovered completely and ran off
He began to mend but was still too feeble to search for food
He was cured instantly by another animal
He wandered off and was never seen again

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "invalid" mean in "the grass that grew round the invalid"?
options: A worthless document
A sick or infirm person or animal
A young animal
A skilled hunter

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why did the Stag ultimately die?
options: A predator found him while he was helpless
His visitors ate up the grass he needed, leaving him with nothing once he was well enough to feed himself
He caught a second, more severe illness
He wandered too far from the clearing

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Wild animals should never visit the sick
Well-meaning visitors can cause real harm through carelessness
Illness always leads to death in the forest
Stags are more vulnerable than other forest animals

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happened to the Stag before he lay in the clearing?
options: He fell sick
He was injured by a hunter
He lost a fight with another stag
He was abandoned by his herd

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how many of the visiting beasts nibbled the grass?
options: Only a few of them
None of them
One and all of them
Only the largest ones

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was left within the Stag's reach after the visits?
options: Plenty of grass
Not a blade of grass
A small patch of grass
Only dry leaves

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "fodder" mean in "go in search of fodder"?
options: Shelter from rain
Food for animals
A mate
A hiding place

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the fable suggest about the visiting beasts' intentions?
options: They meant to help but did not consider the harm they were causing
They deliberately plotted to starve the Stag
They wanted to steal the Stag's territory
They were testing the Stag's strength

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Stag recovers from illness thanks to his friends' care
A Stag falls sick, and visiting beasts unintentionally strip his grass bare, so he starves once he is well enough to need it
A Stag is nursed back to health by a single loyal friend
A Stag drives away visitors who try to eat his grass
